vascular_cognitive_impairment.summary: No disease-modifying therapy exists for vascular cognitive impairment; management is control of the vascular risk factors, secondary prevention matched to the mechanism, review of the anticholinergic burden, and treatment of coexisting Alzheimer pathology where biomarkers support it.

output.impression: A three-component gait disorder: the short-stepped wide-based pattern with dual-task decay is the higher-level gait disorder of small-vessel disease; mild truncal instability reflects alcohol-related cerebellar involvement; and visual dependence with a positive Romberg reflects the sensory neuropathy. Each contributes to the falls.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not attribute the whole syndrome to alcohol in a patient whose decline progressed while intake fell and whose blood pressure was never controlled
Do not give glucose-containing fluids before thiamine in a patient with chronic alcohol use
Do not prescribe benzodiazepines outside a managed withdrawal in a patient with this falls risk
Do not treat an unconfirmed Korsakoff syndrome as established in the absence of confabulation and with normal mamillary bodies
Do not omit the vascular risk-factor treatment because the alcohol history is prominent
required_recommendations: Establish whether the decline continued during the period of reduced alcohol intake, because that is what separates the two attributions
Look for the Korsakoff phenotype explicitly — confabulation, storage-type amnesia, mamillary body atrophy — rather than assuming alcohol explains any cognitive deficit in a drinker
Document the cognitive profile formally and exclude reversible causes including thiamine and B12
Obtain brain MRI and read it for two processes rather than one
Separate the components of the gait disorder, since each has its own management
Treat the untreated hypertension, which is driving the component that is still progressing
Refer for alcohol cessation and provide the vitamin replacement that prevents Wernicke syndrome

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no diagnostic role in vascular cognitive impairment; it belongs to the differential of a rapidly progressive or fluctuating course (Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, non-convulsive status, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy), none of which is present here

A presynaptic dopaminergic study answers the Lewy-body question, not the vascular one, and there is no spontaneous parkinsonism, no fluctuating cognition with hallucinations and no REM sleep behaviour disorder
Cardiac sympathetic imaging is a test for dementia with Lewy bodies and for autonomic failure; it says nothing about cerebrovascular disease

An untargeted paraneoplastic or autoimmune-encephalitis battery in a chronic stepwise decline with a hypertensive imaging burden is the archetypal expensive miss; the indication for those assays is a subacute multidomain syndrome
The MRI already obtained answers everything a CT could and more: CT cannot show microbleeds or cortical superficial siderosis, so it cannot grade the vascular burden this diagnosis rests on
There is no embolic lesion pattern to explain: the burden here is small-vessel, and a structural cardioembolic source would not account for it
Prolonged rhythm monitoring is for an unexplained embolic infarct pattern; in pure small-vessel disease it changes nothing about the diagnosis or the treatment

accepted: Vascular dementia — subcortical ischaemic (small-vessel) type from untreated hypertension, with a coexisting alcohol-related cerebellar syndrome and sensory polyneuropathy contributing to the gait disorder

differential.key_features: Twenty-five years of heavy intake makes this a genuine contender and it may contribute, but the deficit progressed across a year of substantially reduced intake, there is no Korsakoff phenotype, and the Fazekas 3 burden with three lacunes is sufficient on its own
No ophthalmoparesis, no acute confusional episodes in the history, no confabulation, normal mamillary bodies and no periaqueductal signal change; thiamine is low-normal on supplementation
Cue-responsive recall, preserved hippocampi and an executive-predominant profile
No stigmata of chronic liver disease, no asterixis, normal ammonia not required given the absence of any clinical or biochemical evidence of decompensation
B12 214 pg/mL is low-normal and warrants correction, but cannot account for a Fazekas 3 burden with three lacunes

key_clinical_evidence: The temporal test is decisive: alcohol-related cognitive impairment stabilises or improves with reduced intake, so progression across a year of substantial reduction implicates a second, still-active process
Korsakoff syndrome has a positive phenotype — dense storage amnesia with confabulation and mamillary body atrophy — and its absence is informative rather than merely unproven
Two comorbid processes can each be identified on one MRI: a Fazekas 3 small-vessel burden and superior vermian cerebellar atrophy have different causes and different implications
Untreated hypertension in a patient whose drinking has fallen is the actionable driver, and adherence is the intervention
Attributing everything to alcohol is the failure mode this case is built around: it removes the treatable vascular diagnosis from view

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The decline continued through a year of substantially reduced intake, there is no Korsakoff phenotype, and the Fazekas 3 burden with three lacunes is independently sufficient — alcohol contributes to the cerebellar and neuropathic findings

clinical_assessment.impression: MoCA 21/30 with an executive and retrieval profile, no confabulation and no amnestic-confabulatory syndrome. Alcohol-related cognitive impairment typically stabilises or improves with abstinence; continued progression across a year of substantially reduced intake, in a patient with untreated hypertension, points to an additional vascular process rather than to alcohol alone.

labs.interpretation: MCV 99.4 fL with a GGT of 118 U/L and ALT 46 U/L reflects continuing alcohol intake. B12 214 pg/mL is low-normal and worth correcting. Thiamine is low-normal on supplementation with no clinical Wernicke syndrome. TSH, folate, RPR and HIV are normal or negative. LDL 128 mg/dL is above target. Nothing here identifies a reversible cause sufficient to explain the syndrome.

specialized_test.impression: A subcortical executive profile with preserved recognition memory and no confabulation. Korsakoff syndrome would present with a dense storage-type amnesia and confabulation, neither of which is present; the pattern matches the small-vessel burden.

key_educational_points: Progression during a period of reduced drinking is the argument that separates vascular from alcohol-related cognitive decline
Korsakoff syndrome should be diagnosed on its positive features, not assumed from a drinking history

A prominent alcohol history is the commonest reason a treatable vascular diagnosis is missed

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Fabio Greco is a 66-year-old former lorry driver who attends with his brother. He drank between 100 and 120 grams of ethanol daily for about twenty-five years and has cut down to around forty grams in the past year. Over three years his brother has watched him become slower, more forgetful and less able to organise: he cannot manage his own benefits paperwork, forgets to pay for things, and has twice left the flat with the gas on. He is unsteady, particularly in the dark, and has fallen twice. He also reports numbness in his feet going back several years. His brother is clear that the cognitive decline has continued during the past year in which drinking has fallen substantially, which is the observation that brought them to the clinic: they expected improvement and did not see it. He had a withdrawal seizure six years ago and two withdrawal episodes. He denies double vision, has never had an episode of confusion with unsteadiness and eye movement problems, and has never been admitted for encephalopathy. His blood pressure has been recorded above 160 systolic on most visits and he takes amlodipine irregularly. There are no hallucinations, no fluctuations and no dream enactment.

neurological_exam.additional: No hepatomegaly, no spider naevi, no palmar erythema. No asterixis. Frontal release signs absent. Palpable pulses, regular at 80.
neurological_exam.coordination: Mild bilateral heel-to-shin ataxia with normal finger-to-nose; no intention tremor.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal and reactive. Extraocular movements full with no nystagmus and no gaze palsy. Visual fields full. Face symmetric. Speech normal.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based and short-stepped with mild truncal instability; arm swing preserved. Tandem impossible. Romberg mildly positive.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, oriented to person and place, year correct, date wrong by a week. MoCA 21/30 with losses in trail-making, cube, digit span backwards, serial sevens, fluency (10 animals) and delayed recall (2/5 unaided, 4/5 cued). No confabulation. Insight partial.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk with mild proximal wasting in the legs. Tone mildly increased in the legs. Strength 5/5 apart from 4+/5 hip flexion.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 3+ knees, absent ankle jerks, plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Vibration reduced at the ankles and pinprick reduced to the mid-shin bilaterally, consistent with alcohol-related polyneuropathy.
